turns.text: The aspiration is a regenerative economy where investment does not simply clone the Cabos engine.

turns.text: La Paz would act as services capital and water-energy node, while Comondú keeps room as an agricultural center.

turns.text: Los Cabos remains the tourism engine but under water and power stress.

turns.text: East Cape stays in tension with protected areas, while Todos Santos and El Pescadero form the Pacific amenity spine.

turns.text: Loreto anchors tourism with conservation limits, and Comondú adds production without emptying services elsewhere.

turns.text: Like the desert plants that send roots in every direction so one dry spell doesn't finish them.

turns.text: Mm. A quiet kind of strength.

turns.text: Then the coast doesn't have to carry everything alone.

turns.text: Wait—do you mean the kind of growth that actually stays when the big projects shift?
